messages:
Ana R (ML): Hey all - starting onboarding for <model: open-llm-13b-finetuned-q8> for chat+tooling. I flipped on quantization and function-calling and seeing malformed JSON from assistant when we request structured output. Need a short checklist + a stable prompt template we can test. Anyone worked this flow recently?

Matt G: I did a quick run. Two likely causes: 1) quantized kernels truncating logits for special tokens, 2) prompt/system framing leaking plain-text into JSON.

Sophia (DevEx): Can you paste the exact chat template you're using? small differences in `system` role wording change model behavior.

Ana R (ML): Here's the simplified template we used (first pass):
```
[system] You are a JSON-output assistant. Always respond with valid JSON matching the schema: {"intent": string, "items": [ {"id": string, "score": number} ] }
[user] Summarize the page and return top 3 items.
```
Model returned a message with extra text: "Note: this is approximate" before JSON.

Jordan (Infra): @Ana R (ML) - did you pin the same model binary for the inference worker? quant variants sometimes fall back to FP where kernels differ. Also check `max_new_tokens` + `eos` handling.

Leo (Runtime): Quick checklist I use for chat+tooling bring-up:
- Run `prompt-stability` probe (1000 prompts, varied temps)
- Function-call probe: force `function_call={'name':'none'}` and ensure model respects it
- JSON schema probe: ask for `response_format` with explicit `json_schema` and validate 
- Latency/cold-start with kv-cache enabled

Matt G: For the prompt template, try this minimal structured-output framing that worked for me: 
```
[system] You must ONLY output JSON. Do not include explanations or commentary. Keys: intent(string), items(array of objects with id(string),score(number)). If unsure, return null for that field.
[user] <user text>
```
Also set temperature=0.0, top_p=0.0 for deterministic validation runs.

Sophia (DevEx): I'll add a short test harness to `examples/structured-output` with the above template + a CI job that validates schema (jsonschema). Should I use `chat.completions` or our `responses` API shim for that repo?

Jordan (Infra): Use `chat.completions` for now — function-calling semantics are closer. For Dedicated flows we map that to `/v1/chat` internally.

Ana R (ML): Good call. Couple more things from quant experiments: when using q8/q4 kernels I saw increased token dropout around long system prompts. Actionables:
- Reduce system role length, push constraints into a short `response_format` block.
- Re-run with `kv_cache` on/off to isolate.
- Run small eval suite (SQuAD-like + our internal extractive QA + the tool calling probe).

Leo (Runtime): Example `response_format` snippet to include in system role: 
```
{"response_format": {"type":"json_schema","schema": {"type":"object","properties": {"intent": {"type":"string"}, "items": {"type":"array","items": {"type":"object","properties": {"id":{"type":"string"},"score":{"type":"number"}}}}}}}
```
That helps the model prefer strict JSON tokens.

Matt G: For prioritization: if model passes schema probe + function-call respect + latency SLO, mark high priority for integration. If it fails schema but low cost improvement, deprioritize.

Sophia (DevEx): I'll create a 1-page onboarding checklist and a small repo PR with templates + CI. Assigning myself and @Matt G to review.

Ana R (ML): Thanks — can you also include a short A/B test plan: quant vs fp32 on quality metrics (exact-match, BLEU, hallucination rate)? we'll need to justify rollback criteria.

deploy-bot: Scheduled canary deploy queued for model open-llm-13b-finetuned-q8 at 2024-06-01T18:00Z :rocket:

Jordan (Infra): Final note - add a quick smoke `function_call` that calls a dummy `add_metadata()` function; if the model returns anything but `name: add_metadata` we fail the probe. Keeps tool routing safe.

Ana R (ML): Perfect. I'll collect results and post a short summary in this thread when CI and probes finish. Thanks! :raised_hands:
